title: Streaming TPS Chronicle: portable tokens/sec microbenchmark and regression guard
creator: Ava Morgan
description: Goal: Ship a portable, CI-friendly tokens-per-second (TPS) microbenchmark harness focused on streaming workloads and p95 regression detection across core models. The harness (bench/streaming-chronicle) will run short, reproducible sessions that mimic production streaming patterns, collect tokens/sec and tail latency distributions, and feed results into the regression detector to raise PR-based alerts. Primary consumers: runtime and performance SREs, model onboarding, and release engineers.
updates: 2026-03-05 - Created ticket. Initial scope drafted: streaming runner, synthetic and replay modes, p95 delta alerting, Grafana dashboard tiles.

2026-03-07 - Spike completed: implemented prototype runner that supports repeatable RNG seeds and three load profiles (chat-avg, chat-long, single-turn). Benchmark runner lives at bench/stream-runner in the perf repo.

2026-03-09 - Design review with @Priya Shah (runtime) and @Liam Chen (SRE). Agreed to use Prometheus histograms for per-request latency and a tokens-emitted counter for TPS. Decided to decouple KV-warmup phase from measurement window.

2026-03-11 - Integrated with CI: added job perf/streaming-chronicle to nightly perf pipeline. Job runs against pinned model commits and stores JSON artifacts in s3://perf-artifacts/stream-chronicle/{{date}}/.
2026-03-13 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf/pull/12345 (implements sampling harness + baseline comparisons). Requesting review from @Samira Patel and @Noah Kim.

2026-03-14 - Added draft Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/Abc123/streaming-tps-chronicle. CI artifacts hooked to regression detector at https://ops.redwood.ai/regressions/stream-chronicle.
acceptance_criteria: Bench runner executes reproducible streaming workloads (seeded RNG) with configurable warmup and measurement windows
Runner emits Prometheus metrics: tokens_emitted_total, requests_started_total, request_duration_seconds histogram with p50/p95/p99 buckets
Nightly CI job produces JSON artifacts and a CSV summary with model, sequence_length, concurrency, TPS_mean, TPS_p95, p95_delta_vs_baseline
Regression detector flags a PR when p95 increases by >15% vs baseline for two consecutive nightly runs and opens an alert ticket
Dashboard tiles for per-model TPS and p95 trends available in Grafana with links to artifacts
Documentation (Confluence) with runbook, sample commands, and interpretation guide published
Benchmark is portable (Docker image or k8s job) and can be run locally by engineers with a single command
test_plan: Unit tests for runner components and metrics exporter (CI passes)
Replay mode validation: run against a captured 1k-request trace to confirm output matches golden JSON within 2% TPS variance
Synthetic mode validation: run three load profiles across core models (small, medium, large) and assert p95 values are within expected bands from historical baselines
Canary: enable nightly run for a single core model for 3 days, inspect stability, then roll to full core model matrix
Regression detector end-to-end test: inject synthetic 20% p95 inflation in staging artifacts and confirm detector raises a PR alert
implementation_notes: Runner implemented in Go for lightweight concurrency and predictable GC behavior; uses gRPC client against local inference shim
Measurement window defaults: 60s warmup, 120s measurement; configurable per-profile
KV warmup handled by replaying first N tokens of a longest-context sample before starting measurement window
Metrics exported via a /metrics endpoint scraped by Prometheus; artifacts uploaded as ndjson per-request and CSV summaries
CI job stores artifacts in s3 with path: s3://perf-artifacts/stream-chronicle/{{model}}/{{date}}/ and writes a meta.json with runner config
Regression detector compares rolling median of last 5 nightly p95s to new run; threshold and alert policy configurable in ops console
Include quantization and kernel-variant matrix in runs to catch perf regressions specific to build-time changes
Expose a --local mode that runs against a developer laptop with a small token budget and prints a human-readable summary
